# Command line reference

`todonotifier COMMAND [options]`. `python -m todonotifier` does the same. For examples and the output formats, see the [command line guide](../cli.md).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `todonotifier scan` | scan and print the TODOs |
| `todonotifier report` | write the HTML reports |
| `todonotifier notify` | send the digest to the notifiers of the config file |
| `todonotifier init` | create a starter config |
| `todonotifier --version` | Print the version. |

## Flags of `scan`, `report` and `notify`

These flags are shared. A flag beats the config file, which beats the built-in defaults. PATH arguments may be mixed with options.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PATH ...` | Files and directories to scan (default: the `paths` of the config file, else `.`). |
| `--config PATH` | Config file to use instead of looking for .todonotifier.toml or pyproject.toml |
| `--tags TODO,FIXME` | Comma separated tags to look for (default: TODO,FIXME,HACK,XXX) |
| `--ext py,js` | Comma separated file extensions; 'common' is the preset of common languages (default) |
| `--ignore-case` | Match tags case insensitively (todo, Todo) |
| `--no-require-comment` | Also report tags that are not in a comment |
| `--no-gitignore` | Also scan files that .gitignore excludes |
| `--no-blame` | Do not run git blame (no authors, ages or default due dates) |
| `--blame` | Run git blame; the last of --blame and --no-blame on the command line wins |
| `--default-due-days N` | An undated TODO turns stale N days after it was added; 0 disables (default: 90) |
| `--since GIT_REF` | Only report TODOs on lines added or changed since GIT_REF, e.g. HEAD~1 or origin/main |
| `--fail-on {none,expired,stale,any,incomplete}` | Exit with 1 if such a TODO exists: expired (explicit date passed), stale (also default dates), any, incomplete (no owner like @user or TODO(user), or no explicit {date}) |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Show errors only |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show debug logs, and the traceback of unexpected errors |

## `todonotifier scan`

Scan files and directories for TODOs and print them. With no config, all common languages are scanned.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--format {table,json,github,markdown,sarif,html}` | Output format: table, json, github, markdown, sarif, html (default: table) |
| `--output FILE` | Write the result to FILE instead of stdout (for html: the directory for the report files) |

## `todonotifier report`

Scan and write the HTML reports (module-wise, expired by user, upcoming week) to a directory. Same as 'scan --format html'.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--format {table,json,github,markdown,sarif,html}` | Output format: table, json, github, markdown, sarif, html (default: html) |
| `--out`, `--output FILE` | Directory for the report files (default: .report); with another --format, the file to write |

## `todonotifier notify`

Scan, then send the result to every notifier in the [notify.&lt;name&gt;] tables of the config file (slack, teams, webhook, email) and to those added with --slack-webhook-env, --teams-webhook-env and --webhook-url-env. All notifiers are tried; each failure is printed.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--format {table,json,github,markdown,sarif,html}` | Output format: table, json, github, markdown, sarif, html (default: nothing is printed) |
| `--output FILE` | Write the result to FILE instead of stdout (only with --format) |
| `--slack-webhook-env NAME` | Also send to the Slack webhook URL in this variable |
| `--teams-webhook-env NAME` | Also send to the Teams webhook URL in this variable |
| `--webhook-url-env NAME` | Also POST the JSON digest to the URL in this variable |

## `todonotifier init`

Append a commented [tool.todonotifier] section to pyproject.toml if it exists, else create .todonotifier.toml. Never overwrites anything.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--pyproject` | Add the section to pyproject.toml |
| `--standalone` | Create .todonotifier.toml |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | OK. |
| `1` | The `--fail-on` condition was met. For `notify` this wins over a failed notification. |
| `2` | Usage or config error: a bad flag or config file, a path that does not exist, an unknown `--since` ref (or no git repository for it), no notifier configured. |
| `3` | Unexpected runtime error (add `-v` for the traceback), or a notification could not be delivered. |

Errors are one line on stderr, for example `todonotifier: error: Unknown key 'tagz' in pyproject.toml [tool.todonotifier]. Did you mean 'tags'?`.
